articles.title: mRNA Shots Called 'Deadliest Product in History': McCullough Foundation Epidemiologist Names Names, Cites Buried Data
articles.summary: Nicolas Hulscher of the McCullough Foundation laid out a systematic case against mRNA vaccines, flu vaccine fraud, and suppressed cancer research in a long-form interview that mainstream media won't touch. The interview directly challenges the captured consensus on vaccine safety and efficacy, citing epidemiological data the FDA and CDC have refused to act on. If Hulscher's analysis holds, the regulatory agencies responsible for approving these products have blood on their hands.

articles.title: Estrogen, Serotonin, and Endotoxin: The Hormonal Framework Medicine Refuses to Teach
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov breaks down how estrogen dominance, histamine dysregulation, serotonin excess, and endotoxin load interact in ways that mainstream endocrinology systematically ignores — leaving millions misdiagnosed and mistreated. Standard blood panels are designed to miss the problem, and the pharmaceutical solutions offered treat symptoms while worsening the underlying metabolic dysfunction. This is the alternative metabolic framework that threatens the entire hormone therapy and SSRI profit model.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Tyler Shultz Blasts New Holmes Documentary for Sanitizing a Convicted Fraudster
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, the whistleblower who helped bring down Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos, says the new documentary 'You Can See Everything' renders Holmes 'almost unrecognizable' — a carefully managed image rehabilitation that papers over the reality of a medical fraud that endangered patients with false diagnostic results. Shultz risked his career, family relationships, and safety to expose a company that faked blood test data used in real clinical decisions. The documentary's framing, he suggests, lets Holmes off the hook in ways that insult everyone who fought to tell the truth.

articles.title: FTC Catches Martin Shkreli Trading 60 Drug Stocks in Violation of Lifetime Pharma Ban — Contempt Motion Filed
articles.summary: The FTC and seven states allege that Martin Shkreli — already banned for life from the pharmaceutical industry — secretly traded stocks in at least 60 drug companies, making a mockery of the legal guardrails designed to protect patients from predatory pharma actors. The contempt motion exposes how toothless industry bans are when financial incentives remain and enforcement is lax. Shkreli's brazen defiance is a window into an industry where accountability is theater.

articles.title: Brownstone Institute: COVID Accountability Is Not Optional — The Reckoning Has to Come
articles.summary: The Brownstone Institute's Steven Kritz argues that without genuine accountability for pandemic-era policy failures — lockdowns, mandates, suppressed treatments, and agency capture — the institutions that caused mass harm will simply reconstitute themselves and do it again. The piece names the structural corruption at NIH, CDC, and HHS that allowed bureaucratic self-interest to override public health science. No accountability means no deterrence, and no deterrence means the next manufactured crisis will be worse.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Sued After FTC Complaint Exposes Alleged Deceptive Health Product Claims
articles.summary: A securities class action has been filed against Hims & Hers Health following an FTC federal complaint alleging the company misled consumers about its health products — raising serious questions about how telehealth platforms are marketing prescription and compounded drugs with inadequate transparency. The lawsuit implicates company executives in decisions that allegedly prioritized growth over honest clinical disclosure. This is the direct-to-consumer pharma model under legal fire, and it won't be the last.

articles.title: What the Theranos Employee Who Watched the New Documentary Wanted to Scream at the Screen
articles.summary: A former Theranos insider watched the new Elizabeth Holmes documentary and found it so distorted from reality that the reaction was visceral — the film's sympathetic framing erases the lived experience of employees who saw the fraud firsthand and patients who received dangerously inaccurate medical test results. The documentary's approach is being read by those inside the story as narrative capture — the same mechanism by which institutional science suppresses inconvenient truths. When the whistleblowers are more credible than the filmmakers, something has gone deeply wrong.

articles.title: FDA Rubber-Stamps New Hepatitis B Drug — But Who's Asking About the Trial Data They Didn't Publish?
articles.summary: The FDA has approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) for chronic hepatitis B, but the press release buries the fact that it works only in combination with existing antivirals and only in patients without cirrhosis — a narrow population conveniently not highlighted in the headline. Routine FDA approvals increasingly follow a pattern of selective data presentation that inflates benefit and minimizes risk, with full clinical trial datasets rarely made publicly available for independent scrutiny. Until raw trial data is open-sourced, every FDA approval deserves a suppression score.

articles.title: Shkreli Thumbs His Nose at Lifetime Pharma Ban — FTC Says He Traded 60+ Drug Stocks Anyway
articles.summary: The FTC and seven states allege Martin Shkreli violated a court-ordered lifetime ban from the pharmaceutical industry by secretly trading stocks in at least 60 drug companies. If true, it confirms what critics have long argued: pharma's most notorious bad actors operate with impunity while regulators look away. The contempt motion is a rare instance of the system attempting to enforce its own rules against one of its own.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Tyler Shultz Says Holmes Documentary Whitewashes a Fraud That Endangered Patients
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, the whistleblower who helped bring down Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos, says the new documentary 'You Can See Everything' presents a sanitized, almost unrecognizable version of the woman whose fake blood-testing technology put patient lives at risk. Shultz is sounding the alarm that the film rehabilitates a fraudster instead of reckoning with the systemic failures that allowed Theranos to operate for years. The medical establishment and its media allies appear more interested in Holmes' redemption arc than in the patients who were harmed.

articles.title: Estrogen, Histamine, Serotonin: The Metabolic Framework Mainstream Medicine Refuses to Touch
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov breaks down the interconnected roles of estrogen dominance, histamine dysregulation, serotonin excess, and endotoxin load in chronic disease — a framework almost entirely absent from conventional clinical practice. Standard medicine dismisses estrogen dominance when blood levels appear 'normal,' ignoring tissue-level hormonal dynamics that may explain widespread fatigue, fertility collapse, and metabolic dysfunction. This is exactly the kind of mechanistic, non-pharmaceutical disease model that gets no NIH funding and no mainstream coverage.

articles.title: Brownstone Institute Demands COVID Accountability: The Suffering and the Dead Cannot Be Forgotten
articles.summary: Brownstone Institute's Rev. John Naugle issues a moral indictment of the institutions that imposed pandemic policies responsible for documented physical, psychological, and economic harm. The piece refuses to allow a quiet pivot away from accountability for lockdowns, mandates, and suppressed treatments. With no criminal referrals, no congressional action, and legacy media silent, this is one of the few venues keeping the body count in public view.

articles.title: Brownstone Institute: COVID Accountability Is Not Optional — The Reckoning Has Barely Begun
articles.summary: Steven Kritz at Brownstone Institute argues that without real accountability for pandemic-era policy decisions — forced masking, school closures, vaccine mandates, suppression of early treatment — the institutions that caused harm will simply repeat the cycle. The piece names the structural failures inside public health bureaucracies that insulated decision-makers from any consequence. This is the institutional critique that NIH, CDC, and HHS have spent years trying to bury under 'following the science' cover.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Securities Fraud Lawsuit After FTC Complaint — Telehealth's Dark Side Comes Into Focus
articles.summary: A securities class action has been filed against Hims & Hers Health following a sweeping FTC complaint alleging deceptive practices by the company and its executives. The case raises serious questions about whether direct-to-consumer telehealth platforms have been misleading patients and investors alike about the nature and safety of the treatments they prescribe. This is what happens when the 'disruptive health' narrative collides with regulatory reality.

articles.title: Former Theranos Insider Says the New Holmes Film Wanted to Make Him Scream — Here's Why That Matters
articles.summary: A former Theranos employee who lived through the fraud says the Nathan Fielder documentary 'You Can See Everything' is so detached from the reality of what Holmes did that it provoked visceral rage in him. When whistleblowers and insiders are this alarmed by a media rehabilitation effort, it signals an active attempt to rewrite history around a case of medical fraud that endangered real patients. Hollywood is doing what regulators failed to do: giving Holmes a soft landing.

articles.title: HIV Latency Research Reveals Defective Proviruses Drive Immune Reprogramming — A Finding With Major Treatment Implications
articles.summary: New research published in PLOS Pathogens shows that defective, transcriptionally active HIV proviruses — long dismissed as irrelevant junk — can actively reprogram immune cells to help the virus persist despite antiretroviral therapy. This upends a foundational assumption of HIV cure research that has guided NIH-funded strategies for decades. If defective viral remnants are biologically active drivers of immune evasion, the entire cure research pipeline may need to be rebuilt from the ground up.

articles.title: Martin Shkreli Caught Trading 60+ Pharma Stocks Despite Lifetime Ban — FTC and Seven States Demand Contempt
articles.summary: The FTC and seven state attorneys general allege that Martin Shkreli — already barred for life from the pharmaceutical industry — secretly traded stocks in at least 60 drug companies in flagrant violation of court orders. The motion for contempt exposes how industry bad actors exploit regulatory gaps to maintain financial influence over drug markets. If proven, this represents a direct subversion of the enforcement mechanisms meant to protect the public from predatory pharma insiders.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Tyler Shultz Slams Holmes Documentary for Sanitizing a Convicted Fraudster
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, the Theranos insider who risked everything to expose Elizabeth Holmes' blood-testing fraud, says the new documentary 'You Can See Everything' presents an 'almost unrecognizable' version of the woman he watched deceive patients and investors for years. Shultz's critique cuts to the heart of how media narratives can rehabilitate bad actors before accountability is complete. The suppression of accurate scientific fraud history benefits those who profit from blurring the line between innovation and deception.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment Under Fire: Mental Illness Diagnosis Does Not Erase Informed Consent
articles.summary: A damning legal and ethical analysis at Reason magazine challenges the government's expanding authority to forcibly medicate individuals diagnosed with mental illness, regardless of their expressed wishes. The piece names the core tension: if a psychiatric label can strip a person of the right to refuse treatment, the diagnosis itself becomes a weapon of coercion. This argument has been systematically marginalized by a psychiatric establishment with direct financial ties to the drugs being mandated.

articles.title: Estrogen, Serotonin, and Endotoxin: The Metabolic Framework Mainstream Medicine Refuses to Teach
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov lays out a bioenergetic framework linking estrogen dominance, histamine dysregulation, serotonin excess, and endotoxin accumulation to a cascade of modern chronic diseases — a model almost entirely absent from medical school curricula. Standard hormonal panels are exposed as inadequate, routinely missing tissue-level estrogen excess even when blood levels appear normal. This metabolic lens challenges the pharmaceutical model's reliance on symptom suppression over root-cause resolution.

articles.title: Theranos Insider Who Blew the Whistle Says Fraud Documentary Made Him Want to Scream
articles.summary: A former Theranos employee who witnessed the company's fraudulent diagnostic science firsthand says watching the new Holmes documentary produced a visceral reaction of disbelief at how the narrative was framed. The account underscores a recurring pattern: whistleblowers who sacrifice careers and safety to expose medical fraud are then sidelined as entertainment media repackages the perpetrators as complex, sympathetic figures. Scientific fraud in diagnostics has direct patient harm consequences that no documentary softening can undo.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Hit With Securities Fraud Lawsuit After FTC Accuses Company of Deceptive Health Claims
articles.summary: A securities class action has been filed against Hims & Hers Health following an FTC federal complaint alleging the telehealth company made deceptive claims to consumers about its medical products and services. The lawsuit exposes how direct-to-consumer health platforms can monetize patient desperation while misrepresenting clinical evidence. Investors and patients alike were allegedly kept in the dark while executives profited.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment Is Forced Treatment: The State Has No Right to Medicate You Against Your Will
articles.summary: A Reason investigation confronts the government's growing appetite to override patient refusal of psychiatric drugs — a power with no legitimate medical or ethical basis. The piece names the core issue mainstream psychiatry refuses to: coercive treatment is not care, it is control. When diagnosis becomes a mechanism for stripping civil liberties, the entire edifice of psychiatric 'science' deserves scrutiny.

articles.title: Estrogen Dominance, Endotoxin, and the Hormonal Lies Your Doctor Won't Tell You: Georgi Dinkov Breaks It Down
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov lays out a metabolic framework that implicates estrogen dominance, histamine excess, serotonin toxicity, and gut-derived endotoxin as interconnected drivers of chronic disease — a framework almost entirely absent from mainstream clinical practice. Standard hormone panels are exposed as structurally misleading, masking true tissue-level estrogen burden. The implications for fertility, energy metabolism, and psychiatric drug use are enormous and deliberately ignored.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Is the Cancer Signal Medicine Refuses to Treat: What the Research Actually Shows
articles.summary: A deep dive into peer-reviewed research linking chronic mitochondrial dysfunction and systemic inflammation to elevated cancer risk — a metabolic theory of cancer with decades of supporting evidence that oncology's chemotherapy-and-radiation industrial complex has systematically marginalized. The data showing that restoring mitochondrial function can reduce cancer risk is real, reproducible, and almost never discussed in oncology clinics. Follow the funding to understand why.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Tyler Shultz Says Holmes Documentary Sanitizes a Fraudster — The System That Enabled Her Remains Untouched
articles.summary: Tyler Shultz, the whistleblower who risked everything to expose Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos, says the new documentary 'You Can See Everything' presents an 'almost unrecognizable' version of the woman who ran a billion-dollar medical fraud that gave false diagnostic results to real patients. Shultz's criticism cuts deeper than the film: the regulatory apparatus — FDA, investors, board members — that allowed Theranos to operate for years faces zero accountability. The whistleblower paid; the system did not.

articles.title: Martin Shkreli Allegedly Traded 60 Pharma Stocks in Defiance of Lifetime Ban — FTC Wants Contempt Finding
articles.summary: The FTC and seven state attorneys general are moving to hold Martin Shkreli in contempt, alleging he secretly traded stocks in at least 60 pharmaceutical companies despite a court-imposed lifetime ban from the industry. If proven, this is not a rogue actor story — it is a structural story about how pharma insiders operate with near-impunity until the paper trail becomes impossible to ignore. The contempt motion names the trades, the companies, and the timeline the court ban was allegedly violated.

articles.title: FTC Sues Hims & Hers: The Telehealth Darling Built on Deceptive Claims Now Faces Securities Class Action
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health, the telehealth platform aggressively marketed to consumers seeking alternatives to traditional pharma, now faces both an FTC federal complaint alleging deceptive practices and a securities class action lawsuit targeting company executives. The case exposes how 'disruptive' health companies can replicate the same fraudulent playbook as legacy pharma while wearing a consumer-friendly mask. Investors who bought the narrative are now the ones holding the losses.

articles.title: Placental GDF15 Deficiency Drives Fetal Growth Restriction — And the Implications for Miscarriage Research Are Being Ignored
articles.summary: New research in PLOS Biology demonstrates that placenta-specific GDF15 is essential for fetal growth via the hepatic STAT3-IGF2 axis, with low circulating GDF15 clinically linked to fetal growth restriction. This mechanistic pathway has direct implications for understanding pregnancy loss and fetal developmental failure — areas where establishment medicine has consistently failed to pursue biological root causes in favor of managed outcomes. The data is peer-reviewed; the clinical translation is nowhere.

articles.title: HIV Reservoirs Maintained by Defective Proviruses That Rewire Immune Cells — Why ART Will Never Be a Cure
articles.summary: Researchers publishing in PLOS Pathogens show that HIV-infected T cell clones persist not through replication-competent virus but through defective, transcriptionally active proviruses that reprogram host immune cells — a mechanism that antiretroviral therapy cannot touch. This undermines the foundational assumption behind decades of ART-as-functional-cure messaging from NIH and pharmaceutical manufacturers. The HIV reservoir problem is deeper and more structurally intractable than patients are being told.
